name: Re-Invoke: Tool Invocation Rewriting for Zero-Shot Tool Retrieval
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2024 (EMNLP 2024 Findings), pages 4705-4726
authors_affiliation: Yanfei Chen, Jinsung Yoon, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister (Google Cloud AI Research); Devendra Singh Sachan (Google DeepMind); Qingze Wang, Vincent Cohen-Addad, Mohammadhossein Bateni (Google). Primary affiliation: Google (Google Cloud AI Research / Google DeepMind / Google). Correspondence: yanfeichen, jinsungyoon, chenyulee @google.com.
code_url: N/A (no official public code repository announced by the authors in the paper, the ACL Anthology entry, or the Google Research blog post; prompts and pseudo-code are released in the paper appendices A-C only)
task_domain: tool-use (tool/API retrieval for tool-augmented LLM agents); the retrieved tools are consumed by a downstream tool-use agent (ToolLLaMA with DFSDT) for task fulfillment
problem_setting: Offline-indexing + online-inference, single-agent, fully UNSUPERVISED (training-free) tool retrieval. Given a user query and a very large pool of tool documents (16,000+ RapidAPI APIs in ToolBench), the system must retrieve the most relevant tool(s) without any labeled query-tool pairs and without fine-tuning a retriever. Two regimes are addressed: single-tool retrieval and multi-tool retrieval (queries needing several tools/categories). The setting targets three stated challenges: (a) LLM input-token-length limits making it infeasible to list all tools in a prompt, (b) an evolving/dynamic tool pool for which maintaining labels and retraining is impractical, and (c) ambiguous user intents where verbose context obfuscates the underlying tool request. Retrieval is decoupled from the agent and also evaluated end-to-end by plugging Re-Invoke as the retriever in front of a ToolLLaMA+DFSDT agent.
what_is_retrieved: tools (tool documents / tool-API descriptions). The retrievable store is the set of tool documents (each containing tool name, API description, and parameters); these are indexed and the top-k relevant tools are returned for the user query.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed pool of tool documents (ToolBench's 16,000+ RapidAPI APIs; ToolE's 199 tools). The store does not grow from the agent's own experience. Re-Invoke enriches each tool document offline with LLM-generated synthetic queries, but the underlying tool corpus is a static, externally provided document collection.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Both top-k ranking and multi-tool completeness. The primary objective is a fixed top-k ranking (nDCG@5 / recall@5 / nDCG@1 / recall@1). For multi-tool retrieval (ToolBench I2/I3, ToolE multi-tool), the multi-view similarity ranking explicitly aggregates the top tool from each extracted intent so that the complete set of needed tools (one per intent) is recovered, i.e., a completeness-oriented variant of top-k that ensures every distinct intent contributes a retrieved tool.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle is implemented)
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is positioned within tool retrieval, generative document/query expansion, and query-rewriting literature.
retrieval_unit: tool-API / tool document (a per-tool document containing the tool name, API description, and parameters). For indexing, the retrievable unit is an augmented tool document = original tool document concatenated with one LLM-generated synthetic query (m such copies per tool).
index_source: Static corpus enriched offline. Tool documents come from existing benchmarks (ToolBench's RapidAPI APIs; ToolE/MetaTool's 199 tools). During offline indexing, each tool document is expanded with m LLM-generated synthetic queries (generative document expansion) and encoded into the embedding space. No online/test-time induction or write-back; the enriched index is built once offline.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (dense embeddings via Vertex AI textembedding-gecko@003) or flat sparse BM25 index. Per tool, m augmented-document copies are created (document + one synthetic query each) and their embeddings are averaged into a single per-tool representation E_d; the store is a flat collection of these per-tool vectors with no graph/hierarchy.
retriever_type: Dense (Google Vertex AI text-embedding, textembedding-gecko@003) OR sparse (BM25, k=1.5, b=0.75); Re-Invoke is applied on top of either. An LLM (text-bison@001 / gpt-3.5-turbo / Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3) is used for query generation and intent extraction, but the matching itself is embedding/lexical similarity, not LLM-as-retriever or generative tool-as-token.
retriever_learning_signal: none (fully unsupervised / training-free). No retriever is trained: off-the-shelf BM25 and off-the-shelf Vertex AI text embeddings are used, and the LLM components (query generator, intent extractor) are used purely in-context (zero/few-shot prompting) with no fine-tuning and no labeled query-tool pairs.
query_construction: Two-sided rewriting. (Indexing side) Document expansion: LLM reads each tool document and generates m diverse synthetic user queries (high sampling temperature for diversity), each concatenated to the tool document. (Inference side) Intent extraction: LLM rewrites the verbose user query into one or more concise tool-related intents via in-context learning, filtering out extraneous background context; these extracted intents replace the original query for matching.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at inference time, t=0): a single retrieval pass is done per user query, but the query is decomposed into multiple intents and indexing-time keys are multiple synthetic queries per tool (a two-level / multi-view construction rather than per-step retrieval).
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (a single retrieval is performed for the user query before the downstream agent acts; no iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval within the retrieval method).
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once up front for each incoming user query (the standard retrieve-then-act pipeline); there is no confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier trigger.
reranking: Yes, a custom multi-view similarity ranking stage. For each extracted intent, tools are ranked by intent-document cosine similarity; a tuple (reversed rank within intent, similarity score) is formed, and the maximum tuple across intents is taken per tool so that the top tool from each intent is aggregated until k tools are retrieved. It is an intent-aware multi-view aggregation rather than a cross-encoder or RRF reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Query-side refinement via intent extraction (the verbose user query is distilled into clean tool-related intents, removing irrelevant background context), plus document-side enrichment. No post-retrieval distillation/compression of the retrieved tool documents themselves; the multi-view ranking is the main post-similarity processing.
tool_document_engineering: Synthetic-query augmentation (generative document expansion): for each tool document, an LLM generates m diverse synthetic queries the tool could answer, and each is concatenated to the original tool document to create augmented documents. Per-tool embeddings are computed as the mean over the m augmented-document copies. An ablation shows appending synthetic queries to the document beats replacing the document with synthetic queries only, and that more synthetic queries (1->5->10) and mean (vs max) aggregation improve nDCG@5.
index_content_separation: N/A / No explicit lightweight-index-then-content separation. The full augmented tool document is embedded and stored; there is no progressive-disclosure split between a light retrievable index and heavy on-demand content (the tool documents are short, e.g., name+description+parameters).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Tool corpus drawn from RapidAPI hub (ToolBench's 16,000+ real-world APIs) and ToolE/MetaTool tools; integration in the end-to-end setting is via the ToolLLaMA + DFSDT agent calling RapidAPI tools. The method is motivated by an evolving tool pool and avoids retraining (so it adapts to new tools by indexing their documents), but the indexing itself is offline/static with no live CRUD auto-sync, MCP, or function-calling protocol described.
tool_dependency_awareness: No explicit inter-tool dependency modeling. Retrieval treats tools independently per intent; multi-tool queries are handled by extracting multiple independent intents and retrieving one tool per intent, not by modeling output-of-A-feeds-B dependencies, shared auth, or prerequisite graphs.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation for a downstream tool-use agent: the top-k retrieved tools are provided to a ToolLLaMA+DFSDT agent which then plans and executes tool calls. The retriever narrows the 16,000+ API search space to a relevant candidate set; the agent uses these retrieved tools to fulfill the instruction. No fine-tuning; retrieved tools enter the agent's prompt/action space.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan: a single retrieval pass selects candidate tools, then the agent (ToolLLaMA with Depth-First Search-Based Decision Tree, DFSDT) plans/searches over those tools to complete the task. Retrieval is a front-end stage, not interleaved per planning step nor embedded inside the agent's tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer (retrieval is a one-shot front-end stage producing the candidate tool set for the whole query; it is not interleaved per CoT step or per tool-call within the downstream DFSDT rollout).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; no retrieved case is adapted/revised). The closest analog is intent extraction, which rewrites the query rather than adapting a retrieved case.
retrieved_item_representation: raw tool documents (structured tool/API descriptions: tool name, API description, parameters in JSON-like form) injected into the downstream agent; on the index side these are augmented documents (tool document + synthetic query) embedded into vectors.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: tool-level descriptive documentation (per-tool capability description / API spec), i.e., a tool-API document rather than a raw trajectory, distilled strategy, or reusable workflow.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Intent extraction as a noise/distractor filter: the LLM intent extractor removes extraneous background context from verbose, ambiguous user queries so the retriever matches on the true underlying tool request (the motivating Fig.1 failure: 'planning a trip to France' masking the real 'improve French language skills' intent). On the index side, document expansion with diverse synthetic queries provides generative pseudo-relevance feedback to better distinguish highly similar tools. No retriever-aware training or learned relevance evaluator.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural memory that the system writes to; only a static, offline-enriched tool-document index).
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills at test time; the enriched tool index is built once offline and is not updated from agent execution.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store does not grow during deployment from the agent's own experience; new tools would be incorporated by indexing their documents offline (re-running query generation), not via online write-back.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back of agent experience). The Limitations section notes that using the downstream agent's execution results as feedback to refine intent extraction is left to future work, confirming no such feedback/write-back exists in the current method.
failure_experience_usage: N/A (no experience/memory storage, so neither successful nor failed trajectories are stored or retrieved).
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries; the offline-built index is static and not mutated by the system after construction).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is a fixed similarity-based top-k (dense or BM25) with a deterministic multi-view ranking rule; it is not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent, single-retriever pipeline; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing (the tool index is a shared external resource but not a shared experiential memory).
benchmarks: ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023; subsets I1, I2, I3) and ToolE (Huang et al., 2023, the MetaTool benchmark; single-tool and multi-tool splits) for retrieval evaluation. End-to-end pass-rate evaluation on six ToolBench subsets: I1-Instruction, I1-Category, I1-Tool, I2-Instruction, I2-Category, I3-Instruction. Data statistics: ToolBench I1 (87,419 queries / 10,439 tools), I2 (84,815 / 13,142), I3 (25,251 / 1,605); ToolE single-tool (20,550 queries / 199 tools), ToolE multi-tool (497 queries / 199 tools).
benchmark_family: tool (ToolBench; ToolE/MetaTool). Tool/API retrieval and end-to-end tool-use benchmarks over the RapidAPI ecosystem (16,000+ APIs) and the MetaTool tool set.
baselines: Unsupervised retrieval baselines: (a) BM25 sparse retrieval (k=1.5, b=0.75); (b) dense retrieval with Google Vertex AI textembedding-gecko@003; (c) HyDE (Gao et al., 2022) on both sparse (BM25) and dense (Vertex AI) settings, generating a hypothetical tool document per query via text-bison@001. End-to-end baselines: ToolLLaMA+DFSDT agent with (i) the reference tool set without a retriever and (ii) ToolLLM's supervised API retriever (Sentence-BERT trained on labeled query-tool pairs).
key_metrics: Retrieval: nDCG@5 (primary), plus nDCG@1, recall@1, recall@5; round-trip consistency recall@10 for the query generator. End-to-end: pass rate (% of instructions completed within budget, per ToolLLM, using gpt-3.5-turbo as evaluator).
headline_result: On ToolE, Re-Invoke achieves a 20% relative improvement in nDCG@5 for single-tool retrieval and a 39% relative improvement for multi-tool retrieval over the best baseline (fully unsupervised). Concretely (dense, text-bison@001 backbone), ToolE single-tool nDCG@5 0.7821 (Re-Invoke) vs 0.6522 (Vertex AI dense baseline) and ToolE multi-tool 0.7231 vs 0.5296. End-to-end, Re-Invoke as retriever raises average ToolBench pass rate to 56.07% vs 52.63% (ToolLLM's trained retriever) and 52.13% (reference tools, no retriever).
ablations: (A) Component ablation (Vertex AI dense): query generator and intent extractor each help individually and combine best (e.g., ToolE single-tool: baseline 0.6522 -> +query generator 0.7813 -> +intent extractor 0.6756 -> both/Re-Invoke 0.7821; ToolBench I2: 0.3880 -> 0.4135 -> 0.5157 -> 0.5379). Intent extractor gives no gain on ToolBench I1 because its APIs are under the same tool so per-intent retrieval overlaps; query generator dominates on ToolE (short docs, names+descriptions only), intent extractor dominates on multi-tool/verbose ToolBench I2/I3. (B) Appending synthetic queries to the document beats using synthetic-query-only (e.g., I1 0.6286 vs 0.4924; ToolE single 0.7813 vs 0.7535), showing replacement causes information loss. (C) More synthetic queries help: 1 -> 5 -> 10 queries (I1 0.5962 -> 0.6242 -> 0.6286; ToolE single 0.7388 -> 0.7777 -> 0.7813). (D) Mean aggregation beats max similarity aggregation across datasets. Backbone-LLM robustness: similar gains with text-bison@001, gpt-3.5-turbo, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3. Round-trip consistency recall@10 confirms query-generator effectiveness, lower on larger toolsets (I1/I2).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (nDCG@1/@5, recall@1/@5, round-trip recall@10) are reported separately from end-to-end task performance (pass rate on the ToolBench agent), explicitly decoupling retrieval quality from downstream task success.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Retrieval-stage (process-level) quality is measured by ranking metrics (nDCG/recall) and round-trip consistency recall; downstream outcome is measured by agent pass rate. No fine-grained per-step reasoning-faithfulness metric beyond these.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Framed as eliminating training/labeling cost: Re-Invoke is fully unsupervised, avoiding the production cost of maintaining labeled query-tool pairs and continuous retraining of a tool retriever as the tool pool evolves. It scales to a vast pool (16,000+ APIs) by narrowing the candidate set before the agent acts, mitigating LLM input-token limits and lost-in-the-middle issues. The added cost is offline LLM calls for synthetic-query generation per tool and one online LLM call for intent extraction per query; no explicit latency or dollar-cost numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Retrieval reported primarily at top-5 (nDCG@5 / recall@5) and top-1; the algorithm retrieves a specified number k of tools via Argmax over the multi-view ranking score, aggregating the top tool per extracted intent until k tools are collected. Indexing uses m synthetic queries per tool (default m=10, ablated over 1/5/10). No explicit token budget for the downstream prompt is stated beyond using the retriever to fit within LLM input-length limits.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (empirical method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (Re-Invoke reuses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). It evaluates on ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023; 16,000+ RapidAPI APIs; I1/I2/I3 splits with 87,419 / 84,815 / 25,251 queries and 10,439 / 13,142 / 1,605 tools respectively) and ToolE/MetaTool (Huang et al., 2023; 199 tools; single-tool 20,550 queries, multi-tool 497 queries / 994 labeled pairs), both providing ground-truth query-tool pairs.
builds_on: Generative document expansion (Nogueira et al., 2019 Doc2Query; Lewis et al., 2021 PAQ; Ma et al., 2023a) for synthetic-query indexing; HyDE (Gao et al., 2022) and Query2doc (Wang et al., 2023) / query-expansion and LLM query-rewriting lines (Jagerman et al., 2023; Mao et al., 2023; Ma et al., 2023b) as the rewriting-pipeline lineage; tool-documentation-for-tool-use (Hsieh et al., 2023; Patil et al., 2023 Gorilla) and ToolBench/ToolLLM (Qin et al., 2023, ToolLLaMA + DFSDT) as the tool-retrieval and downstream-agent substrate; off-the-shelf BM25 (Robertson et al., 2009) and Vertex AI text embeddings as retrievers.
contrasts_with: Supervised/trained tool retrievers that learn from labeled query-API pairs (ToolLLM's Sentence-BERT API retriever (Qin et al., 2023); Kong et al., 2023 TPTU-v2; Gao et al., 2024 Confucius) -- Re-Invoke is fully unsupervised. Generative query-expansion / pseudo-relevance-feedback methods (HyDE, Query2doc) -- Re-Invoke emphasizes query UNDERSTANDING (intent extraction) rather than query expansion, and combines it with document expansion. LLM-agent-as-retriever approaches that list a limited tool set in-prompt -- Re-Invoke retrieves from a vast (16,000+) pool.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). A 2024 zero-shot/unsupervised tool-retrieval method that fuses generative tool-document expansion (Doc2Query/PAQ lineage) with LLM intent extraction (query-rewriting lineage) and a multi-view intent-based ranking, positioned against trained tool retrievers (ToolLLM) and HyDE-style query expansion; a tool-document-engineering successor to Tool Documentation (Hsieh et al., 2023) and Gorilla for scalable tool retrieval.
